rows.why: S1 sets the CSV layout, and its first-row header is exactly what item 1 asks about. The pick emits 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created', which matches. Items 4 (BOM), 2 (row order) and 5 (CRLF) also cover parts of S1, and their picks agree too, but item 1 is the closest fit to the header-and-rows layout.

S2 is about how values are formatted for people to read. Item 9 asks how the creation time is formatted, which is the most specific match on the list. S2 expects the UTC date only (YYYY-MM-DD), but the pick writes the full toISOString() value with the time part. Item 8 (missing title written as empty) also fits part of S2 and agrees. No item asks how statuses are labelled ('On hold' and so on); item 11 is about which statuses are valid, not how they are written.
Item 3 asks what an empty list produces. The pick returns the BOM and the header row only, which is what S3 expects.

Item 6 asks how fields with separators are escaped. The pick quotes them per RFC 4180 and doubles embedded quotes, which covers commas, quotes and CR/LF. It says nothing about S4's leading or trailing spaces (RFC 4180 itself does not require quoting those), and it does not say whether fields that need no quoting are left unquoted. So the pick is too vague to say whether it matches S4 in full.
Item 7 asks how formula-like leading characters are handled. The pick writes the value as is, with no prefix. S5 requires a leading single quote before =, +, -, @, tab or CR.

Item 10 asks what happens with bad row data: unknown status, invalid or negative counts, filled greater than openings, or an invalid date. The pick throws an Error naming the requisition id, which is what S6 expects.
